title: Move the lore check gate to lore 0.12.0 and re-export the .lore schemas
description:
Filed by the QCLI-421 0.12.0 bump session (2026-09-29). The `lore check` gate pins the newest PUBLISHED lore this repository has been measured against; it is at 0.11.0 (QCLI-394) and the next published version is 0.12.0, from the pair release this bump prepares. Not started, and it cannot start before lore 0.12.0 is on npm.

THE INVARIANT, from the workflow's own header: the number never moves without the committed `.lore` schemas being regenerated by that same lore. A pin-only change reds the gate whenever the new lore changes schema generation, which reads as a broken pin rather than a pending regeneration.

CHOOSE THE LANDING SHAPE BY MEASURING FIRST, not by picking the shape that reads simplest. Run the new lore with `npx --yes @opum-ai/lore@0.12.0` rather than upgrading the shared global binary, and measure the regenerated tree under BOTH pins. The header names three cases: same PR when the regenerated tree also passes the old pin; two steps when it passes the old pin but the new pin reds the old tree; atomic when the regenerated tree fails the old pin, because no order of two landings is green then. QCLI-394 moved 0.9.2 to 0.11.0 in that third shape, and its own correction records that the list used to word this case as "two steps otherwise".

A `lore check` exit 7 (indeterminate: a schema it cannot attribute) means stop and report, never delete or re-export past it.

This gate cannot detect its own staleness -- it runs AT the pinned version, so it is self-consistent by construction and stays green as the pin falls behind. The QCLI-358 weekly detector is the thing that compares the pin against npm, and it will open one lore-pin-stale issue; this task is the other half, the move itself.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The pin in .github/workflows/lore-check.yml names 0.12.0, and the committed .lore schemas are the ones 0.12.0 generates -- landed in the shape actually measured to be green, not the shape that read simplest.
The regenerated tree was measured under BOTH pins before the landing shape was chosen, and both measurements are recorded on this task with their exit codes.
lore check exits 0 on the merged result at the new pin, and the required context reports green on the head that lands it.
Once npm serves lore 0.12.0, the QCLI-358 detector reports the pin current rather than opening a lore-pin-stale issue.
